findings: The completed-wait hook replaces the production signal handler, so real SIGTERM does not set the production interrupted latch.
The injected header is included before required setup constants, the guard is auto-defined instead of compiler-supplied, and byte/string counting fails after partial output creation.
Missing-setup ignores diagnostic write failure and the partial case does not bind the actual 383 retained bytes.
The oracle consumes invented flat fields rather than the retained production report/artifact/raw-wait schema and expects wrong READY state for the completed-wait case.
Packet, patch and header identities and exact generated-diff boundaries are not frozen.
Build, run and root ownership paths are plans or disabled placeholders and cannot satisfy the reviewed isolation/evidence contract.
independent_review.archive_limitation: The archive contains the candidate source but not raw stderr from the zero-test Python invocation; that invocation outcome is dispatcher-recorded rather than archive-proven.
